US corporate debt issuance is skyrocketing:

US investment-grade corporate bond sales are expected to rise +$37 billion YoY in November, or +27%, to $175 billion, the highest for any November on record.

This would mark a +$76 billion, or +77%, increase from November 2024 level.

To put this into perspective, the 5-year average before 2025 was $104 billion.

By comparison, US investment-grade bond issuance stood at ~$100 billion in October.

As a result, US investment-grade bond sales have risen to a record $1.76 trillion YTD, already surpassing the full-year 2025 total of $1.75 trillion.

Meanwhile, over $300 billion in AI-related corporate bonds have been issued in global investment-grade markets so far in 2026, almost 3 times the total for all of 2025.

AI spending is fueling an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

posts.text:
For most of the 10+ years I spent at Sprott, we had a running inflation/deflation debate that often got rather heated. 

Each time the economy and the stock market collapsed, Eric grew very weary of a deflationary depression.  

I always argued (to the point of nearly being fired on my early years) that the central bankers will bail out their banker buddies as they always have.  That they will create money and monetize any bad debts they see fit.  That they can and will push prices up of anything they choose.  Preventing deflation is rather easy if you really want to be a reckless government with a supportive central bank.   

Maintaining reasonable employment levels is at the core more important than inflation targeting. 

Still, the drawdowns in these periods of retrenchment can be extremely nasty.  Like we are seeing now.  Gold and silver can drop 50-70% no problem.  It’s happened over and over again as golds moved from $20 to $6000 in the century.  

All this said,  I always felt long term inflation is the greatest worry.  Especially for younger people 

But now, I’m starting to get really concerned about the 3 massive deflationary forces that are building up.   Robotics, Ai and nanotechnology.  The combo is going to super deflationary. 

Huge job losses… and frankly I don’t think anyone has a clue where people getting laid off will end up getting hired.  It’s easy for those doing the firing to say that it will sort itself out.  But, as companies cut 10’s of thousands of high paying middle aged workers and our youth graduate school with completely useless degrees…. Well, Houston… we got a problem. 

I think the response will be printing and bailing along with infrastructure spending.  

Governments will have no choice but to fund these massive projects and use freshly printed money to do it. 

This remains core to my investment thesis.  We must prepare for the downside and expect high volatility.   But, position for what sectors will experience growth and margin expansion.

Quality producers of commodities and nano tech companies with valuable patent portfolios will ultimately prove to be the best safe haven over this next decade.  Just like how the tech stocks mostly had a lost decade post Y2K with many failing.  We will see a lot of struggles in today’s bubble stocks

We likely have barely heard of the companies that will be the best for performing stocks of the next 10-15 years.  Many are probably still private and just getting started.  :)
